candidates.name: Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma
support_spans: several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
a left nasal mass was noted
a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components completely opacifying the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging results are consistent with a highly vascular tumor, such as Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma, which is common in teenage males but can also occur in females.

candidates.name: Fibrous Dysplasia
support_spans: bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
candidates.why: The presence of bony changes and remodeling suggests a possible diagnosis of Fibrous Dysplasia, which can cause expansion and thinning of bone.

candidates.name: Giant Cell Tumor
support_spans: tissue analysis showed spindle cell process in a patternless arrangement with significant multinucleated giant cells
candidates.why: The biopsy results showing significant multinucleated giant cells are consistent with a Giant Cell Tumor, which can occur in the maxillary sinus.
